findings.title: Delayed-stop execution time is misdescribed for active playback
findings.detail: TR-TAPE-EDGE-001 ac-02 says running state is retained before the stop executes at t+32000, and TEST-TAPE-RAMP-001 ac-02 fixes observations at deadline-1, deadline, deadline+1. Native read_bit re-arms the stop alarm and then reschedules the same alarm to the next read gap, so with an attached image in START, FORWARD or REWIND the motor stops at the first datasette alarm at or after t+32000 (bounded by DATASETTE_MAX_GAP=100000 scaled by tape speed) and pulses continue until then. Exact t+32000 holds only without an active read-alarm stream (no image, STOP or RECORD mode). Mock fixtures derived from the TR text would encode the wrong expectation.
findings.evidence: datasette.c:729-745 (unset, re-arm at motor_stop_clk), :806-851 (alarm_set to next gap), :735-739 (stop only when maincpu_clk >= motor_stop_clk), alarm.h:176-183 (pending alarm modified in place).
findings.recommendation: Operator decision: amend TR-TAPE-EDGE-001 ac-02 and TEST-TAPE-RAMP-001 ac-02 to distinguish stop timing with and without an active read stream; add a named active-playback MotorOff case. No rewrite performed by this review.

findings.title: FORWARD/REWIND fast-wind scheduling (MOTOR_DELAY_FAST=1000) not covered
findings.detail: FORWARD and REWIND schedule the datasette alarm at maincpu_clk+1000 regardless of motor state; the unset branch in datasette_forward/datasette_rewind never runs because mode is assigned before the call. A subsequent motor-on therefore does not add a 32000 startup alarm while that alarm is pending. No AC or named case covers this timing, so a mock using 32000 for fast-wind would pass.
findings.recommendation: Operator decision: add fast-wind timing criteria and named cases.

findings.title: Running-motor semantics for recording are undefined
findings.detail: Writes are accepted as soon as the motor flag is set at motor-on (no startup wait) and continue during the 32000-cycle delayed-stop window until the stop executes. AC say running motor without defining it; no named case writes during the startup window or the delayed-stop window.
findings.evidence: datasette.c:1182-1191 (motor flag set immediately), :1303-1305 (write eligibility checks the motor flag only), :735-739 (flag cleared only when the stop executes), FIXME at :1010-1013.
findings.recommendation: Operator decision: define running motor for recording and add window cases.

findings.title: RECORD pressed while the motor already runs is not enumerated
findings.detail: Accepted RECORD calls tap_reset_gap (last_write_clk=0) but not start_motor, so the first qualifying 0-to-1 edge measures write_time from clock 0 and emits a long gap of maincpu_clk (low 24 bits in v1/v2). Covered only generically by first-write state and known native quirks; the named case list does not distinguish motor-on-then-RECORD from RECORD-then-motor-on.
findings.recommendation: Operator decision: enumerate both orderings in Recording_GapEncodingAndFailures.

findings.title: Machine motor-line and write-line wiring uncovered; related requirement contradicts pinned source
findings.detail: The corrected AC cover sense input and read-pulse routing only. C64 motor is CPU port $0001 bit 5 (active low, and DDR input yields motor on) and the write line is bit 3 (DDR input yields line high, so DDR changes can create write edges); VIC-20 motor is VIA1 PCR CA2. The only existing C64 motor wiring requirement, FR-TAP-001 ac-01, says bit 3, contradicting c64pla.c. FR-TAP-001 is outside the approved five and unchanged.
findings.evidence: c64pla.c:77-89, vic20via1.c:185-203, live FR-TAP-001 ac-01. Managed C64MemoryMap.ApplyCassetteMotor already uses bit 5.
findings.recommendation: Operator decision: add machine motor/write wiring criteria and correct FR-TAP-001 through a separately approved delta.

verifiedNativeFacts: MOTOR_DELAY 32000 for PLAY and RECORD, MOTOR_DELAY_FAST 1000 for fast wind (datasette.c:62-63).
Startup alarm at clock+32000 only when no datasette alarm is pending (datasette.c:1006-1008).
Motor-on aborts a pending stop and starts the motor only from stopped state (datasette.c:1182-1193).
Motor-off on a running motor sets the stop deadline once; repeated motor-off does not extend it (datasette.c:1195-1201).
RECORD ignored without image and with read-only image; accepted RECORD asserts sense (datasette.c:1091-1099, 1149-1151).
C64 sense: CPU port $0001 bit 4 reads low when sense asserted and DDR bit 4 is input; pullup 0x17 (c64pla.c:65-66, c64mem.c:222, 1012-1015).
VIC-20 sense: VIA1 port A bit 6 low when asserted, masked by DDRA (vic20via1.c:246-251).
Read pulses: C64 CIA1 FLAG (c64datasette.c:39), VIC-20 VIA2 CA1 falling (vic20datasette.c:40).
Write eligibility: image, RECORD mode, motor flag; 0-to-1 transition; last write bit updated unconditionally (datasette.c:1303-1321).

Gap encoding: write_time below 7 carried; below 2047 one byte write_time/8 with remainder carry (7 emits 0x00); 2047 and above zero byte plus 3-byte length for v1/v2; failures stop the tape; has_changed only after success (datasette.c:1215-1290).
